conflicts.point: Whether national legislatures can implement binding compute caps at 10^26 FLOPs without restricting public code repositories or harming open-source innovation.

positions.stance: National legislatures can set legal compute limits at 10^26 FLOPs and exempt smaller research clusters, protecting open-source builders while constraining massive frontier scaling.

Compute caps create a compliance cliff that commercial entities will circumvent by fragmenting training runs or routing through proxy clusters, while statutory exemptions fail to prevent administrative burdens on open innovation.

verdicts.conflict: Whether national legislatures can implement binding compute caps at 10^26 FLOPs without restricting public code repositories or harming open-source innovation.
verdicts.rationale: The accelerationist and skeptic claims provide concrete enforcement failures, showing how compliance cliffs and verification bureaucracy make statutory exemptions unworkable in practice. The safetyist claim relies on abstract regulatory design without specifying how to prevent workload fragmentation or audit burdens.
verdicts.whatWouldChange: Evidence of successful regulatory frameworks that enforce compute caps on large labs while maintaining zero administrative overhead for open-source developers.
